Consumer F1/proof1.1 instantiate the supplier real scalar reference triple with P_r contained in the space, bounded DOFs on W^{r+1,2}, and its dual nodal basis. Boundedness/unisolvence are assumptions, not inferred from arbitrary DOFs; global boundary mapping remains separate.

Consumer F3/proof3.1 uses p=2, orders0/1 and r+1, including determinant cancellation; both affine directions are available. Choice assumption is retained in consumer.

Supplier gives unique linear interpolant and exact reproduction on its FE space under bounded DOFs. Consumer F1/proof1.1 uses the finite dual-basis sum and Iq=q for P_r contained in that space, yielding the error after subtracting q. No point-evaluation boundedness is assumed beyond the explicit bounded-DOF hypothesis.

Supplier with order parameter r+1, p=2 and s=0,1,r+1 gives one moment polynomial q in P_r and full W^{r+1,2} error bounded by the top seminorm. Consumer F2/proof2.1 applies that same q to both terms of proof1.1. The full-order case justifies the interpolant term, not merely an L2/H1 estimate. This imports no fractional dual approximation.

Actual page context imports six typed convex-analysis/prox interfaces, with sixteen exact item uses checked below. Closed epigraph convention, positive prox parameter, finite-domain subgradients and locally proved block-model recurrences are preserved. Full-vector proximal-gradient/FISTA or eta-subgradient rates are not inferred for block updates with mere model-gap certificates; finite-horizon block theorems prove their own accepted-per-history convolutions.

Consumer F2/proof1.1 takes continuous slices of closed epigraphs to obtain closed weak sublevels, then neighborhoods around the finite block minimizer. It retains an existing unique continuous minimizer map; does not derive it from closedness or invoke a generic sequential-topological equivalence.

Consumer F1/proof1.1–3.1 uses nonempty finite domains, convexity and closed epigraphs of the finitely many g_i. Finite choices establish properness and explicit product neighborhoods establish epigraph closedness, including infinite-value points; no unrecorded countable choice or arbitrary sequential closure is used.

Consumer Definition assumes each block penalty proper closed convex under the supplier epigraph convention and a finite feasible initial point. It defines accepted model gaps and explicit failure/budget statuses rather than inferring objective accuracy or future iterates from finite execution.

Supplier Definition identifies the set of global minimizers of g(u)+||u-v||²/(2t), with its separately justified singleton convention. Consumer optional G_M stopping map uses t=1/M_i and v=x_i-grad_i f/M_i; no full-vector proximal-gradient rate is imported.

A finite-domain segment and t-downarrow0 give each all-z block subgradient inequality; infinite-value comparison points are handled automatically. No nonconvex/nonseparable stationarity extension is made.

Consumer F1/proof1.1–2.1 obtains -grad_i f in each block subdifferential and sums the separable inequalities; proof3.1 adds the convex-f tangent inequality for global minimality. It does not use an epsilon-subgradient rate theorem.

Consumer proof2.1 separately supplies exact/nonexact objective descent from the block smoothness/model-gap inequality; firm nonexpansiveness or a full-prox convergence rate is not silently transferred.

Consumer F4/proof1.1 assumes each penalty proper closed convex on its positive-dimensional Euclidean block, so completion of the square is an admissible prox problem with t=1/M_i>0. No existence from mere value-gap output is asserted.

Supplier Definition identifies the set of global minimizers of g(u)+||u-v||²/(2t), with its separately justified singleton convention. Consumer F3/proof1.1 completes the square in the selected block model with t=1/M_i>0 and v=x_i-grad_i f/M_i; the unchanged other blocks contribute constants.

Consumer L1/proof3.1 first obtains E_{n+1}<=(1+Lambda h)E_n+(M/2)h² with E0=0 on N=Km steps, Lambda=2L/(1-|a|)>=0, T=Nh; applies p=1,C0=0,C=M/2 and both Lambda branches. Consumer F2/Verification3.1–3.2 uses exactly numerical exact-start output minus exact next value. Its breakpoint-crossing RK4 computation gives +(1+tau)h²/24 rather than O(h5), explicitly rejecting smooth-RHS order transfer. This is a local defect example, not a higher-order DDE convergence theorem.
